cases.reason: pydna's golden_gate_assembly has no way to say 'this part cannot take part': it finds no join and silently returns nothing, the same answer it gives for a set that is merely incomplete. From the model: a part with no site is never cut, so it contributes no ligatable end and no circle can contain all three parts. Expected: no circular product, and the engine must name the part.

cases.label: BsaI, p3 ends two bases into its right overhang
cases.reason: p3's second BsaI site points off the 3' end of the molecule: the top-strand cut lands two bases before the end and the bottom-strand cut falls past it, so only two of the four overhang bases exist. pydna/Biopython and the plugin need not even agree on whether that counts as a cut, and pydna has no way to report the situation. Either way the model gives the same answer: a 2-base end (or an uncut part) cannot anneal to the 4-base ends of p1 and p2, so no circle can contain all three parts. Expected: no circular product, and the engine must report ends of different lengths or an unusable part.

cases.label: BsaI, one part, both overhangs TAAA
cases.reason: pydna routes a one-fragment reaction through SingleFragmentAssembly, which also reports insertion and inversion products, so its product list is not comparable. The answer follows from the construction instead: cutting the part releases a middle fragment whose top strand is ov + body + ov with a 4-base 5' overhang at each end, and closing it writes the shared overhang once, giving the circle ov + body.
